insight.title: Why Total Comfort Makes You Feel Sluggish
insight.subtitle: How subtle physical friction keeps your brain alert
insight.notificationHook: Comfort quietly drains your mental alertness

sections.text: You sit in an ideal chair, in a quiet room, with zero disruptions—yet you feel surprisingly sluggish. High alertness doesn't come from total comfort; it requires subtle environmental resistance to stay active.

In nature, trees grown inside windless greenhouses develop weak trunks that collapse under their own weight. Gentle wind triggers stress responses that build structural density. Your nervous system operates on the exact same principle.

When your body experiences complete physical ease, your brain interprets the environment as passive and lowers your overall energy levels. Introducing mild physical friction instantly signals your mind to wake up.
Try this today: When you feel mentally sluggish today, roll your shoulders back and take one deep breath.
Your mind doesn't thrive in total ease; it thrives on gentle resistance.
